topics.label: Request Lifecycle
topics.desc: End-to-end path of a request through listener, parsing, routing, middleware, handler, and response that frames all server design.

topics.label: Threading vs Event Loop
topics.desc: Thread-per-request, thread pools, and single-threaded event loops trade memory and context-switch cost against I/O concurrency.

topics.label: App Servers & Gateways
topics.desc: Process managers and protocol bridges like WSGI/ASGI, FPM, and Unicorn that host application code behind a web server.

topics.label: Middleware Pipeline
topics.desc: Composable layers wrapping handlers for auth, logging, compression, and error handling, ordered as an onion of cross-cutting concerns.

topics.label: Routing & Dispatch
topics.desc: Mapping method and path patterns to handlers via trie or regex matching, with params, wildcards, and route precedence.

topics.label: Config & Dependency Injection
topics.desc: Wiring services, settings, and connections via DI containers and layered config to keep handlers testable and environment-portable.

topics.label: REST Constraints
topics.desc: Statelessness, uniform interface, layered system, and cacheability that define REST and distinguish it from arbitrary HTTP APIs.

topics.label: Resource Modeling
topics.desc: Designing nouns, URIs, and resource hierarchies so that operations map cleanly onto HTTP verbs and collection semantics.

topics.label: Methods & Status Codes
topics.desc: Correct verb semantics (idempotency, safety) and precise status codes that let clients reason about outcomes without parsing bodies.

topics.label: Pagination & Filtering
topics.desc: Offset and cursor pagination plus filtering and sorting conventions that keep large collection endpoints performant and stable.

topics.label: API Versioning
topics.desc: URI, header, or media-type versioning strategies that let APIs evolve without breaking existing consumers.

topics.label: OpenAPI & Schemas
topics.desc: Machine-readable contracts driving docs, client generation, validation, and mock servers as a single source of API truth.

topics.label: Idempotency Keys
topics.desc: Client-supplied keys letting servers dedup retried unsafe requests so a flaky network never double-charges or double-creates.

topics.label: RPC Fundamentals
topics.desc: Calling remote procedures as if local via stubs and serialization, trading network transparency for tighter client-server coupling.

topics.label: gRPC & Protobuf
topics.desc: HTTP/2-based RPC with Protocol Buffers IDL, code generation, and streaming, favored for low-latency internal service calls.

topics.label: GraphQL Schema
topics.desc: Strongly typed schema with queries, mutations, and subscriptions letting clients request exactly the fields they need in one round trip.

topics.label: Resolvers & N+1
topics.desc: Field resolver functions that fetch data, plus DataLoader batching to defeat the N+1 query explosion they naturally cause.

topics.label: Schema Federation
topics.desc: Composing a unified GraphQL graph from independently owned subgraphs so teams ship schema slices without a monolithic gateway.

topics.label: IDL & Code Generation
topics.desc: Interface definition languages that generate type-safe clients and servers, eliminating hand-written marshalling and drift.

topics.label: REST vs RPC vs GraphQL
topics.desc: Choosing an API paradigm by weighing coupling, caching, over/under-fetching, and tooling against the consuming clients' needs.

topics.label: AuthN vs AuthZ
topics.desc: The core split between proving identity (authentication) and granting permissions (authorization), enforced at distinct layers.

topics.label: Sessions & Cookies
topics.desc: Server-side session state keyed by signed cookies, with attributes like HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite governing browser security.

topics.label: Tokens & JWT
topics.desc: Self-contained signed claims enabling stateless auth, with tradeoffs around revocation, expiry, and storage that bite if mishandled.

topics.label: OAuth2 & OIDC
topics.desc: Delegated authorization flows and the identity layer atop them that power third-party login and scoped access-token issuance.

topics.label: RBAC & ABAC
topics.desc: Role- and attribute-based models for expressing who may do what, scaling permission logic beyond ad-hoc per-endpoint checks.

topics.label: API Keys & mTLS
topics.desc: Service-to-service credentials and mutual TLS that authenticate machine clients where interactive login flows do not apply.

topics.label: Secrets & Key Rotation
topics.desc: Securely storing, distributing, and rotating signing keys and credentials so a leak has a bounded blast radius and lifetime.

topics.label: Cache Layers
topics.desc: Client, CDN, reverse-proxy, application, and database caches stacked so each tier absorbs load before the slower one below it.

topics.label: Caching Strategies
topics.desc: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, and write-behind patterns that trade consistency, latency, and write amplification.

topics.label: Cache Invalidation
topics.desc: TTLs, explicit purges, and event-driven busting that keep cached data fresh, the famously hard half of caching.

topics.label: Distributed Caches
topics.desc: Redis and Memcached clusters providing shared, low-latency state for sessions, rate limits, and hot data across server fleets.

topics.label: HTTP Cache Semantics
topics.desc: ETags, Last-Modified, and Cache-Control directives the server sets to let proxies and clients reuse responses safely.

topics.label: Connection Pooling
topics.desc: Reusing established database and HTTP connections to amortize handshake cost and cap concurrent backend resource usage.

topics.label: Rate Limiting & Throttling
topics.desc: Token-bucket and sliding-window limits protecting APIs from abuse and overload while signaling clients with 429s and headers.

topics.label: Message Queues
topics.desc: Brokered queues decoupling producers from consumers, smoothing load spikes and enabling retry and durability for slow work.

topics.label: Task Queues & Workers
topics.desc: Background job systems (Celery, Sidekiq) that offload expensive work from the request path onto pools of worker processes.

topics.label: Pub/Sub & Events
topics.desc: Fan-out event distribution where many independent consumers react to published facts without the publisher knowing them.

topics.label: Delivery Guarantees
topics.desc: At-most/at-least/exactly-once semantics and the idempotency and dedup needed to tolerate redelivery in real systems.

topics.label: Scheduled & Cron Jobs
topics.desc: Time-triggered and recurring tasks with distributed locking to ensure a job fires once across a horizontally scaled fleet.

topics.label: Retries & Dead Letters
topics.desc: Backoff retry policies and dead-letter queues that isolate poison messages so a single bad payload cannot stall a pipeline.

topics.label: Webhooks & Callbacks
topics.desc: Outbound HTTP notifications to subscribers, with signing, retries, and idempotency to deliver events to external systems reliably.

topics.label: Service Boundaries
topics.desc: Decomposing a system along business capabilities so each service owns its data and changes independently of others.

topics.label: Service Discovery
topics.desc: Dynamic registries and DNS that let services locate healthy instances of peers as they scale, move, and fail.

topics.label: API Gateway
topics.desc: Edge entry point unifying routing, auth, rate limiting, and aggregation so clients face one facade over many services.

topics.label: Service Mesh
topics.desc: Sidecar proxies handling mTLS, retries, and traffic policy, moving cross-service networking concerns out of application code.

topics.label: Inter-Service Comms
topics.desc: Choosing synchronous calls versus async messaging between services, balancing latency coupling against availability coupling.

topics.label: Circuit Breakers
topics.desc: Circuit breakers, bulkheads, timeouts, and retries that stop a failing dependency from cascading into total outage.

topics.label: Sagas & Distributed Tx
topics.desc: Saga orchestration and choreography with compensating actions to maintain consistency without distributed two-phase commit.

topics.label: ORMs & Data Mapping
topics.desc: Object-relational mappers translating rows to objects, easing CRUD but risking the impedance mismatch and hidden query cost.

topics.label: Repository & DAO
topics.desc: Abstracting persistence behind a collection-like interface so domain logic stays ignorant of storage and is unit-testable.

topics.label: Query Builders & Raw SQL
topics.desc: Composing parameterized queries programmatically or in raw SQL when ORM abstractions obscure performance-critical access.

topics.label: Schema Migrations
topics.desc: Versioned, reversible schema changes applied in lockstep with code so deploys evolve the database without manual surgery.

topics.label: Transaction Management
topics.desc: Controlling commit boundaries, isolation, and unit-of-work scope in application code so multi-step writes stay atomic.

topics.label: N+1 & Eager Loading
topics.desc: Diagnosing lazy-load query explosions and applying eager loading or batching to collapse them into bounded queries.

topics.label: Pooling & SQL Injection
topics.desc: Connection-pool exhaustion and injection risks at the data layer, prevented by bounded pools and parameterized statements.
